t: For purposes of implementing the provisions of, and amendments made by, this title and titles I and II of this division, other than section 203, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide for the transfer, in appropriate part from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund established under section 1817 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395i) and the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund established under section 1841 of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1395t), of $45,000,000 to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Program Management Account for the period of fiscal years 2007 and 2008.

fable.w: This section only directs an internal transfer of funds from Medicare trust funds to the CMS Program Management Account to pay for implementation. The word "implementing" might suggest rulemaking, but the section itself neither authorizes regulations nor provides for any consultation, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Every actor involved is a federal official or a federal account.
fable.s: the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide for the transfer, in appropriate part from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund

opus.w: This section only directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to transfer $45,000,000 from the Medicare trust funds to the CMS Program Management Account for fiscal years 2007 and 2008. Mentioning federal agencies and trust funds does not bring in anyone outside the federal government. No one outside the government is consulted, heard, or given a right to object or sue. Like the appropriations provision in Example 1, this is purely about funding.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** One tempting reading is that the section involves CMS and the Medicare trust funds, which serve the public, so outsiders might seem involved. That reading fails. The section only tells the Secretary of HHS to move $45 million from the Medicare trust funds to a CMS account. Every actor is inside the federal government. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes an internal transfer of funds between federal trust funds and a federal agency account. All entities involved (the Secretary of HHS, the Trust Funds, and CMS) are part of the federal government. There is no consultation, coordination, or interaction with any outside party such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide for the transfer, in appropriate part from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund established under section 1817 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395i) and the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund established under section 1841 of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1395t), of $45,000,000 to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Program Management Account
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that transferring funds between federal trust funds and a federal agency account involves some form of coordination or decision-making that could be construed as participation. However, this is purely an internal fiscal transfer within the federal government. There is no consultation with, or coordination involving, any entity outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). The actors involved are the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund, the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund, and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, all of which are inside the federal government.
